decisions.decision: Declare the representative Provider as a new top-level field representative_provider with the value "claude" in contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json (the capability declaration set), NOT in contracts/release-contract/foundation.json. contracts/release-contract/foundation.json must not be edited by this task.
decisions.rationale: internal/release.CompileContract (internal/release/release.go line 149) decodes foundation.json with decoder.DisallowUnknownFields(), and internal/release/contract_baseline_test.go assertion (a) deliberately proves that an unknown top-level field IS rejected. Adding representative_provider to foundation.json therefore turns TestCompileFoundationBaselineContract red unless the anonymous struct in internal/release/release.go gains the field in the same change; internal/release/** is held by another task right now and is a prohibited path here. The declaration set is the other half of the same versioned Release Contract (bound by contract_ref == foundation.json id and by equal release strings, both already asserted by TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline (c)), it is the half that already declares external_dependencies.providers per capability, and it is read only by internal/contracts through the restricted schema validator, which tolerates additive optional fields. So the declaration lands where the provider facts already live, at zero cost to any prohibited path. release-contract.md section 3's phrase "Release Contractで定めた代表Provider" is satisfied because the declaration set is part of the Release Contract, not a separate artifact.

decisions.decision: In contracts/schemas/capability-declaration-set.json add representative_provider as an OPTIONAL property (not added to "required") of type string with enum ["codex", "claude", "opencode"]. Do not add it to "required".
decisions.rationale: The schema has additionalProperties:false, so the property must be declared or the instance is rejected. Keeping it out of "required" is what makes the change backward compatible: contracts/fixtures/valid/capability-declaration-set.json does not carry the field and must keep validating, and TestSchemasAndFixtures validates every schema against exactly one valid and one invalid fixture. Presence is instead enforced where it is actually required - on the Foundation Repository's own declaration set - by a new assertion in internal/contracts/release_contract_test.go, so a third-party declaration set is not forced to name a representative Provider it does not have.

decisions.decision: Give the new enum genuine negative coverage two ways: (i) add "representative_provider": "gemini" to contracts/fixtures/invalid/capability-declaration-set.json, and (ii) add a dedicated assertion in internal/contracts that takes contracts/fixtures/valid/capability-declaration-set.json, sets representative_provider to "gemini" in a decoded copy, re-encodes it and requires Validate to reject it.
decisions.rationale: The existing invalid fixture already fails for two other reasons (kind is "not-a-capability-declaration-set", release is "latest"), so adding a bad enum value to it proves nothing on its own - the fixture would still be rejected if the enum keyword were absent. Mutating a copy of the VALID fixture is the only way to prove the enum itself does the rejecting. Both are cheap; (ii) is the one that cannot pass vacuously.

decisions.decision: Add to internal/contracts/release_contract_test.go, inside TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline, four new assertions: (k1) foundation-capabilities.json declares representative_provider and its value is "claude"; (k2) the declared value appears in external_dependencies.providers of every capability that declares a non-empty providers array; (k3) each of cap-autonomous-resolution, cap-shared-resource-allocation and cap-provider-operation declares external_dependencies.providers exactly equal to ["codex", "claude", "opencode"] in that order; (k4) if foundation.json ever gains a representative_provider field it must equal the declaration set's value.
decisions.rationale: (k1) turns the declaration from a comment into a machine-checked fact. (k2) forbids naming a representative Provider that the contract does not actually declare as a dependency. (k3) is the anti-weakening guard this task exists to protect: promoting a capability by deleting codex or opencode from its providers array is exactly the substantive contract weakening Sol prohibited, and a pin test is the only thing that makes that prohibition survive the people who come later. Three Provider live remains V2-028's work in M6. (k4) makes the eventual migration of the field into foundation.json (which requires a one-field change to internal/release/release.go, see d1) forward compatible instead of a split brain.

decisions.decision: Add a new schema contracts/schemas/provider-preflight.json with kind const "provider-preflight", required [schema_version, id, kind, created_at, correlation_id, task_id, provider, limits, environment, rollback, verification, approval] and optional [expires_at, notes]. Shapes: provider = {name: enum[codex,claude,opencode], version: pattern ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$, executable_path: pattern ^/[^\u0000]{1,512}$}; limits = {max_invocations: integer minimum 1 maximum 64, max_total_cost_usd: number minimum 0 maximum 100, worst_case_reservation_usd: number minimum 0 maximum 100, currency: const "USD", window: enum[total], ledger_path: pattern ^/[^\u0000]{1,512}$, enforced_by: string, fail_closed: const true}; environment = {base_names: array of string pattern ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$, granted_names: array of the same shape}; rollback and verification reuse deployment-preflight.json's shapes verbatim (rollback {trigger, argv, completion_conditions}; verification items {name, argv, expected, read_only const true}); approval = {approver: email pattern, approved_at: date-time, approval_reference, scope, subject_path: pattern ^\.agents/v2/packets/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.json$, subject_digest: pattern ^[a-f0-9]{64}$}. Every keyword used is one internal/contracts/validator.go actually implements: $ref, const, enum, type, required, properties, additionalProperties:false, minItems, items, minLength, maxLength, pattern, format, minimum, maximum. maxItems, oneOf, if/then and dependentRequired are NOT implemented and must not appear.
decisions.rationale: Same shape as deployment-preflight.json so a reader who knows one knows the other, but the target/limits halves are replaced: deployment-preflight.json's target requires image_digest and plan_digest, which are Google Cloud artefacts a Provider invocation does not have, which is precisely why it cannot be reused. minimum/maximum are verified present in validator.go (they are already used by work-order.json's timeout_seconds), so the numeric ceilings are schema-enforced rather than merely conventional. approval.subject_path plus approval.subject_digest is what makes the approval verifiable: the ledger check can recompute sha256 of the named packet file and refuse an approval that was given for different text. environment.base_names / environment.granted_names carry the two-channel credential boundary as data without using any forbidden word.

decisions.decision: The strings "password", "credential", "raw_prompt" and "raw_provider_output" must not appear anywhere in contracts/schemas/provider-preflight.json, in any case. In particular do not name a field credential_scopes, credential_names or granted_credentials; use environment.granted_names.
decisions.rationale: TestSchemasRejectSensitiveFieldNames walks every *.json under contracts/schemas and fails on a lowercased substring match of exactly those four strings. It is a text scan, so a comment or a description string would trip it too.

decisions.decision: Provider preflight records live in a NEW directory .agents/v2/provider-preflight/, never in .agents/v2/preflight/.
decisions.rationale: CheckDeploymentPreflightLedger validates EVERY *.json under .agents/v2/preflight/ against contracts/schemas/deployment-preflight.json and returns an error for anything that does not validate. A provider-preflight record dropped into that directory would therefore turn the four existing TestDeploymentPreflightLedger* tests red. A sibling directory is additive, is still covered by ci/components.json's task-ledger root .agents/** (so no ci/components.json change is needed), and is still covered by .gitleaks.toml's path prefix \.agents/v2/.*.

decisions.decision: Add validateProviderPreflight to internal/contracts (new file internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go) and dispatch to it from Validate's kind switch in internal/contracts/validator.go with case "provider-preflight". It enforces the four rules the restricted keyword subset cannot express: (1) limits.worst_case_reservation_usd > 0 and <= limits.max_total_cost_usd; (2) limits.ledger_path must not be inside the repository root marker .agents/ and must not be a relative path; (3) approval.approved_at must not be later than created_at; (4) if provider.name == "claude" then environment.granted_names must be empty.
decisions.rationale: Rule 4 is the machine-checked form of the fact that the claude CLI reads its own on-disk credential store: the Secret Broker has nothing to hand it, so a record that claims otherwise is describing a different design and must be refused. Rule 2 keeps the cost ledger out of the repository and out of any workspace by construction. Rules 1 and 3 close the two ways a record can be internally incoherent while still schema-valid. Dispatching from the same switch means the rules also run for the fixtures inside TestSchemasAndFixtures, so the invalid fixture can exercise them.

decisions.decision: Add CheckProviderPreflightLedger(root string) error to internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go, structurally mirroring CheckDeploymentPreflightLedger: every *.json under <root>/.agents/v2/provider-preflight/ must validate against contracts/schemas/provider-preflight.json and its filename must begin with its own task_id; then for every entry of .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose component begins with "provider-live-", exactly one record must share the entry's task_id, the evidence file named by the entry's path must carry an artifact_refs entry with artifact_id "provider-preflight" whose sha256 equals sha256 of that record file's bytes, and the record's approval.approved_at must be strictly earlier than the evidence's observed_at. Additionally verify sha256 of the file named by approval.subject_path equals approval.subject_digest. A missing or empty directory, and an index with no provider-live- component, are both a pass.
decisions.rationale: This is the mechanical form of "human approval precedes any billed side effect", identical in structure to the invariant V2-013 already proved for Google Cloud, so a reader has one pattern to learn rather than two. The digest binding is what makes it non-forgeable in both directions: the evidence cannot point at a record that was edited after the fact, and the record cannot claim an approval that was granted for a different Work Order. Passing with zero records is required so this task can merge before V2-017 ever runs.

decisions.decision: Add to internal/contracts a new test file internal/contracts/provider_preflight_test.go with five top-level tests, named after the deployment ones so the pairing is obvious: TestProviderPreflightLedgerPassesWithNoRecords, TestProviderPreflightLedgerRejectsMissingRecord, TestProviderPreflightLedgerRejectsDigestMismatch, TestProviderPreflightLedgerRejectsApprovalAfterObservation, TestProviderPreflightLedgerPassesWithAWellFormedRecord. Each builds its own root under t.TempDir() with a copy of contracts/schemas/, exactly as internal/contracts/deployment_preflight_test.go already does; none of them writes into the real .agents/v2/.
decisions.rationale: The three failures Sol named (record absent, artifact_refs digest mismatch, approval added after the fact) are the three ways this gate can be defeated, so each gets its own test rather than one test with three branches - a single test that fails for any of three reasons cannot tell you which guard regressed. Copying the deployment test's temp-root technique keeps the real ledger untouched, which matters because .agents/v2/evidence/ is being edited concurrently by another task.

decisions.decision: Amend docs/architecture/roadmap.md with exactly four line edits and no others: line 103 "### M3: One Runner・Codex vertical slice" -> "### M3: One Runner・代表Provider vertical slice"; line 109 "- Codex Adapter" -> "- 代表Provider Adapter（Release Contractのrepresentative_providerで宣言、現在はclaude）"; line 117 "- Codex実物のPreview capabilityが成功する" -> "- 代表Provider実物のPreview capabilityが成功する"; line 161 "- Claude Adapter、opencode Adapter" -> "- 代表Provider以外のAdapter（Codex、opencode）". Lines 157 and 168-171 are NOT edited: M6's heading and its four completion conditions, including "共通adapter変更を3 Providerすべてで実証する", stay exactly as they are.
decisions.rationale: M3's completion conditions name no Google Cloud resource and no specific Provider except through the word Codex, so replacing that word with the contract-declared role is the whole change; anything more is scope creep. M6 has to stop claiming the Claude Adapter as its own deliverable now that M3 ships it, but its completion conditions are the three-Provider obligation itself and weakening them is exactly what Sol prohibited. Leaving the M6 heading alone also avoids touching a heading that other documents may reference.

decisions.decision: Amend docs/architecture/release-contract.md section 3 by appending one parenthetical to the existing bullet "- Provider非依存機能は、Release Contractで定めた代表Providerによる実行を確認する", naming where the declaration lives: "（代表Providerはcapability declaration setのrepresentative_providerで宣言する）". Do not touch section 7 or any other section.
decisions.rationale: Section 3 currently defers to a declaration that did not exist anywhere, which is why the representative Provider was ambiguous in the first place. One clause naming the field turns a dangling reference into a resolvable one. This is not a contract change - the obligation is unchanged - it is the first entry of a declaration the contract always required.

decisions.decision: Plan for no .gitleaks.toml change, but measure instead of assuming. Every value this task commits under .agents/v2/ is either a 64-hex digest (already allowlisted) or a short non-secret-shaped string, and no field name introduced here contains any generic-api-key trigger keyword (access, api, auth, key, credential, creds, passwd, password, secret, token). Run devbox run --pure -- make secrets after committing. Only if it actually reports a finding may .gitleaks.toml gain a third allowlist, and then it must be the same AND-conditioned shape as the existing two, scoped to paths ['''\.agents/v2/.*'''] plus a single anchored value regex, accompanied by a positive control commit proving a real secret of a neighbouring shape is still reported.
decisions.rationale: V2-042 already paid for this lesson: OR-conditioned allowlists silently suppress real findings, and an allowlist added without a positive control is untested. Since the measurement is cheap and the change may well be unnecessary, the honest order is measure first. Note also that gitleaks git scans every ref in the repository, so a finding may originate from a sibling branch rather than from this task's own bytes; V2-042's evidence records the git commit-tree isolation technique for telling the two apart.

decisions.decision: The approval block of any provider preflight record is supplied by the human owner, never invented by the implementing agent. This task writes NO record into .agents/v2/provider-preflight/; it only delivers the schema, the validation and the ledger check. V2-017 writes the single record, and its approver, approved_at and approval_reference must be handed to it.
decisions.rationale: An agent that writes its own approval has built a rubber stamp, not a gate. Keeping .agents/v2/provider-preflight/ empty at the end of this task is also what proves the zero-record pass path (d9) on the real repository rather than only in a temp dir.

risks: The declaration lands in foundation-capabilities.json rather than foundation.json because internal/release/release.go decodes the latter strictly and is held by another task. A reader looking only at foundation.json will not see the representative Provider. Mitigated by assertion (k4) and by the release-contract.md pointer (d12); the eventual move is a separate, sequenced task.

TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline is one large test function; adding four assertions to it increases the blast radius of a single failure. Accepted because splitting it is a refactor this task did not ask for, and because each new assertion carries its own message naming which of k1-k4 failed.

The provider-preflight ledger check is dead code until V2-017 writes the first record. Its only live exercise on the real repository is the zero-record pass path. Mitigated by the four temp-root negative tests (d10), which are what actually prove the guard bites.

gitleaks git scans all refs in the shared repository, so make secrets can be red for reasons that have nothing to do with this task. Do not add an allowlist to silence a finding whose file is not one of this task's own paths; report it instead.

.agents/v2/evidence/index.json is being edited concurrently. Appending one entry is safe only if no other entry's bytes are touched; a whole-file rewrite (even a semantically identical reformat) will conflict or clobber.
